borrow_mut.title: How RefCell::borrow_mut works
borrow_mut.description: Changes a value through a shared reference; the borrow rules are checked while the program runs.

slides.caption: Normally you need &mut to change something. RefCell allows it through a shared & reference, and checks the rules at run time instead.
borrow_mut() hands out a mutable borrow and marks the RefCell as borrowed.
push(2) changes the Vec inside. When the borrow ends, the mark is cleared.
A second borrow_mut() while the first is still alive would panic: "already borrowed".
Often combined as Rc<RefCell<T>>: shared ownership and mutation. try_borrow_mut returns an error instead of panicking.

borrow.title: How RefCell::borrow works
borrow.description: Reads the value; any number of readers, but not while someone is writing.

title.text: let c = RefCell::new(5); let r1 = c.borrow(); let r2 = c.borrow();

slides.caption: borrow() gives a shared borrow, like &T, and counts the readers.
r2 borrows too: 2 readers is fine.
A borrow_mut() now would panic, because readers are active.
These are the same rules the compiler enforces for & and &mut, only checked at run time.

set.title: How Cell::set works
set.description: Replaces a Copy value inside a Cell through a shared reference.

slides.caption: Cell never lends out a reference to its inside, so changing it through & is always safe.
get() returns a copy of it: 5.
Cell is for small Copy values like counters and flags; use RefCell for anything bigger.

get.title: How Cell::get works
get.description: Returns a copy of the value inside the Cell.

slides.caption: get copies the value out; the Cell keeps its own copy.
So does the second; the Cell still holds 3.
get needs the value to be Copy. For other types use take(), replace() or a RefCell.

get_or_init.title: How OnceCell::get_or_init works
get_or_init.description: Computes a value the first time it is asked for, and reuses it afterwards.

slides.caption: A OnceCell starts empty and can be filled exactly once.
First call: the cell is empty, so the closure runs and 42 is stored.
Second call: the closure is not run again.
std::sync::OnceLock is the thread-safe version, handy for global settings.

replace.title: How RefCell::replace works
replace.description: Swaps in a new value and returns the old one.

slides.caption: replace borrows mutably just long enough to swap.
take() does the same with the default value.

new.title: How Cell::new works
new.description: A box for a value that can be changed through a shared reference.

slides.caption: Cell gives "interior mutability" for Copy values: you swap whole values in and out.
Cell never hands out references to its contents, so it needs no runtime checks.

cell-replace.title: How Cell::replace works
cell-replace.description: Puts in a new value and returns the old one.

slides.caption: replace is set that also tells you what was there.

take.title: How Cell::take works
take.description: Takes the value out, leaving the default behind.

slides.caption: take works for any type with a Default.
An empty Vec stays in the Cell.
The way to get a non-Copy value out of a Cell.

swap.title: How Cell::swap works
swap.description: Exchanges the values of two Cells.

slides.caption: Both Cells change, using only &a and &b.
Compare std::mem::swap, which needs &mut to both.

into_inner.title: How Cell::into_inner works
into_inner.description: Unwraps the Cell and returns its value.

slides.caption: When you are done sharing, into_inner gives the value back.
RefCell, OnceCell and Mutex have into_inner too.

get_mut.title: How Cell::get_mut works
get_mut.description: Normal &mut access when you own the Cell exclusively.

slides.caption: With &mut Cell, nobody else can look, so a plain &mut reference is fine.
No runtime cost; useful during setup before the Cell is shared.

refcell-new.title: How RefCell::new works
refcell-new.description: A value whose borrowing rules are checked while the program runs.

slides.caption: RefCell lets you borrow mutably through a shared reference; misuse panics instead of failing to compile.
borrow_mut() lends it mutably; 2 is pushed.
Often combined: Rc<RefCell<T>> for shared, changeable data.

try_borrow_mut.title: How RefCell::try_borrow_mut works
try_borrow_mut.description: borrow_mut that returns Err instead of panicking when already borrowed.

slides.caption: Only one mutable borrow, and no shared ones, may exist at a time.
A borrow() is still alive: Err.

try_borrow.title: How RefCell::try_borrow works
try_borrow.description: borrow that returns Err instead of panicking when mutably borrowed.

slides.caption: Any number of readers are fine, but not while a writer exists.
Use it in code that might be re-entered, e.g. callbacks.

refcell-take.title: How RefCell::take works
refcell-take.description: Takes the value out, leaving the default in its place.

slides.caption: Panics if the value is currently borrowed.

refcell-into_inner.title: How RefCell::into_inner works
refcell-into_inner.description: Unwraps the RefCell and returns its value.

slides.caption: Owning the RefCell means no borrows can exist, so unwrapping is always safe.
Rc::try_unwrap(rc).unwrap().into_inner() gets data out of Rc<RefCell<T>>.

replace_with.title: How RefCell::replace_with works
replace_with.description: Computes the new value from the old one, and returns the old one.

slides.caption: The closure sees the current value and returns the replacement.
Panics if the value is borrowed elsewhere.

refcell-swap.title: How RefCell::swap works
refcell-swap.description: Exchanges the values of two RefCells.

slides.caption: Both are borrowed mutably for the moment of the swap.
Panics if either is already borrowed.

oncecell-set.title: How OnceCell::set works
oncecell-set.description: Fills an empty OnceCell; a second set fails.

slides.caption: The first set wins; later ones get their value back in Err.
Already filled: Err(2), the value stays 1.
get_or_init is easier when you can compute the value on the spot.

oncecell-get.title: How OnceCell::get works
oncecell-get.description: The value if it was set, otherwise None.

slides.caption: get just looks; it never fills the cell.

force.title: How LazyCell works
force.description: A value computed the first time it is used.

slides.caption: The closure is stored, and runs only on first access.
Later accesses return the stored value.
std::sync::LazyLock is the thread-safe version, used for globals.

update.title: How Cell::update works
update.description: Replaces the value with the result of a function of the old value.

slides.caption: get, compute, set, in one call.
Only for Copy types, like get().

from_mut.title: How Cell::from_mut works
from_mut.description: Treats a &mut T as a &Cell<T>, so it can be shared and still changed.

slides.caption: Useful when two places need to change the same value.
x is viewed as a Cell.

as_slice_of_cells.title: How Cell::as_slice_of_cells works
as_slice_of_cells.description: Turns &Cell<[T]> into &[Cell<T>]: each element becomes its own Cell.

slides.caption: Lets you read one element and write another without borrow errors.
An alternative to index juggling: here a running sum.

refcell-get_mut.title: How RefCell::get_mut works
refcell-get_mut.description: A normal &mut to the value, when you own the RefCell exclusively.

slides.caption: &mut RefCell already proves nobody else is borrowing.

map.title: How Ref::map works
map.description: Narrows a RefCell borrow down to one part of the value.

slides.caption: The borrow stays active while the narrowed Ref lives.
Keep only a reference to field 1.
Return a borrowed field from a method without exposing the whole RefCell.

filter_map.title: How Ref::filter_map works
filter_map.description: Narrows a borrow to a part that might not exist.

slides.caption: On failure you get the original borrow back.

map_split.title: How Ref::map_split works
map_split.description: Splits one borrow into two borrows of different parts.

slides.caption: Both halves stay borrowed until dropped.

clone.title: How Ref::clone works
clone.description: Makes another shared borrow of the same RefCell.

slides.caption: Written Ref::clone(&r) on purpose, so it is not confused with cloning the value.
Both must be dropped before borrow_mut works again.

refmut-map.title: How RefMut::map works
refmut-map.description: Narrows a mutable borrow to one part of the value.

slides.caption: Only the field is reachable through the new RefMut.

refmut-filter_map.title: How RefMut::filter_map works
refmut-filter_map.description: Narrows a mutable borrow to a part that might not exist.

slides.caption: Err gives the original RefMut back.
Useful for optional fields inside a RefCell.

refmut-map_split.title: How RefMut::map_split works
refmut-map_split.description: Splits one mutable borrow into two mutable borrows of different parts.

slides.caption: The halves do not overlap, so both can be changed.
The same idea as split_at_mut, inside a RefCell.

unsafecell-get_mut.title: How UnsafeCell::get_mut works
unsafecell-get_mut.description: A safe &mut to the value when you own the UnsafeCell exclusively.

note.text: the building block of all cells

slides.caption: UnsafeCell is what Cell, RefCell and Mutex are built on. With &mut, no unsafe is needed.
Shared mutation through UnsafeCell::get requires unsafe code.

unsafecell-into_inner.title: How UnsafeCell::into_inner works
unsafecell-into_inner.description: Unwraps the UnsafeCell and returns the value.

slides.caption: Owning the cell means nobody else can be using it.

unsafecell-new.title: How UnsafeCell::new works
unsafecell-new.description: Wraps a value so the compiler allows mutation through shared references (with unsafe code).

note.text: for building your own cell types

slides.caption: Normal code should use Cell, RefCell or Mutex instead.
get() returns a raw pointer to the value.

oncecell-new.title: How OnceCell::new works
oncecell-new.description: An empty cell that can be filled exactly once.

slides.caption: Fill it later with set or get_or_init.

oncecell-get_mut.title: How OnceCell::get_mut works
oncecell-get_mut.description: A mutable reference to the value, if set.

slides.caption: With exclusive access, the stored value can be changed.
None if the cell is still empty.

oncecell-take.title: How OnceCell::take works
oncecell-take.description: Takes the value out and leaves the cell empty again.

slides.caption: Needs &mut, so nobody else can be reading.
The cell is empty and can be set again.

oncecell-into_inner.title: How OnceCell::into_inner works
oncecell-into_inner.description: Unwraps the cell: Some(value) if it was set.

slides.caption: take() does the same without consuming.

lazycell-new.title: How LazyCell::new works
lazycell-new.description: Stores a closure that computes the value on first use.

slides.caption: The closure runs at most once.

force_mut.title: How LazyCell::force_mut works
force_mut.description: Forces initialisation and gives &mut to the value.

from.title: How Cell::from works
from.description: Wraps a value in a Cell.

refcell-from.title: How RefCell::from works
refcell-from.description: Wraps a value in a RefCell.

as_ptr.title: How Cell::as_ptr works
as_ptr.description: A raw pointer to the value inside the Cell.

slides.caption: Writing through it is allowed (Cell is not Sync).
Each element can then be set separately.
as_slice_of_cells does the same for slices.

refcell-as_ptr.title: How RefCell::as_ptr works
refcell-as_ptr.description: A raw pointer to the value inside the RefCell, bypassing borrow tracking.

slides.caption: Using it while borrowed elsewhere is undefined behaviour.

try_borrow_unguarded.title: How RefCell::try_borrow_unguarded works
try_borrow_unguarded.description: A plain &T without a guard; Err if mutably borrowed (unsafe).

slides.caption: You must ensure no borrow_mut happens while you use it.

unsafecell-get.title: How UnsafeCell::get works
unsafecell-get.description: A raw *mut T to the contents through a shared reference.

slides.caption: Writing is allowed but you must prevent data races and aliasing yourself.
Cell and RefCell wrap this safely.

raw_get.title: How UnsafeCell::raw_get works
raw_get.description: Gets the inner pointer from a *const UnsafeCell<T>, without making a reference.

slides.caption: Avoids creating references to possibly uninitialised memory.

unsafecell-from_mut.title: How UnsafeCell::from_mut works
unsafecell-from_mut.description: Treats a &mut T as a &mut UnsafeCell<T>.

slides.caption: A building block for custom cell types.

lazycell-get.title: How LazyCell::get works
lazycell-get.description: The value if it was already computed; never runs the closure.

lazycell-get_mut.title: How LazyCell::get_mut works
lazycell-get_mut.description: A mutable reference to the value if already computed.
